text:
mika: seeing a big uptick in tiny-pod evictions in ap-southeast1 over the last 10m, looks correlated with warmnode attach heartbeats failing :eyes:
sam: ugh, any recent scheduler changes rolled out?
mika: not on scheduler, but we rolled lease-handshake v2 to canary in ap-southeast1 ~30m ago. eviction rate jumped right after.
devon: can you paste the attach-controller logs?
mika: here's the snippet:```attach-controller warn: lease heartbeat missed for lease-12345, attempt 3/3, failing attach, cause=rpc timeout
I/O timeout during attach: dial tcp 10.23.45.67:10250: i/o timeout```
linh: also seeing increased `attach_latency_ms` on node exporter: median 120ms -> 800ms for the warmnode cohort. network egress in that AZ is noisy.
ops-bot: ALERT: evictions.ap-southeast1 spike — 412 pods evicted in 5m. https://monitoring/redwood/evictions?range=5m :rotating_light:
sam: hmm, heartbeat timing + network blips -> scheduler thinks nodes are stale and triggers preemptive rebinds. That would cause rapid attach/detach thrash and evictions.
devon: investigate scheduler lease timeouts. Current lease TTL is 30s, heartbeat interval 10s. If jitter high, we can get 2 missed beats -> eviction. Maybe increase TTL to 90s for warmnodes as a short-term mitigation.
mika: proposed mitigation: bump lease TTL to 90s in ap-southeast1 only, pause v2 canary, and scale up warmnode pool by +20% for 1h to absorb churn. Thoughts?
linh: +1 to pause canary. But scaling warmnodes will increase costs and might worsen attach queueing. If network is saturated, more nodes could exacerbate. Maybe scale by 10% and also throttle attach concurrency.
oncall: agree pause canary immediately. Can someone run `kubectl rollout undo ds/attach-controller -n kube-system --to-revision=3`? Also add a temporary fallback route for scheduler to avoid immediate preemptions: set preemptWindow to 60s.
sam: I can undo canary now. Doing `kubectl set image ds/attach-controller attach=attach:v3` -> rollback in progress.
mika: thanks. I'm patching scheduler configmap to set leaseTTL=90s and preemptWindow=60s for ap-southeast1. Applying in 2m.
devon: after changes, watch `scheduler.evictions.rate`, `attach_controller.err_rate`, and `node.attach_latency_ms.p50` — post metrics here.
ops-bot: NOTE: deploy started by sam at 6876543290 (rollback attach-controller), deploy finished at 6876543330 :white_check_mark:
mika: scheduler patch applied at 6876543320.
linh: metrics trending: evictions down from 412 -> 78 in the last 5m, attach errors reduced by ~70%, attach_latency p50 -> 220ms.
devon: good sign. Keep monitoring for 30m. We should write a postmortem once stabilized: root cause = heartbeat sensitivity + network egress jitter + aggressive canary.
oncall: creating an incident ticket and assigning follow-ups:
- ops: run network packet capture on warmnode NICs during next window (linh)
- infra: add conservative rollout guard for lease/heartbeat patches (devon)
- cost: estimate impact of temporary warmnode scale-up (mika)
mika: noted. I'll also add a scheduler experiment: make leaseTTL a percentile based on node attach latency so we don't use fixed small TTLs.
sam: thanks everyone. tagging this thread for postmortem notes. :memo:
devon: one more thing — consider adding per-AZ fallback: if attach errors spike, route new tiny pods to other regions rather than mass-evicting. That's more complex but reduces impact.
linh: agreed. I'll run a small chaos test to reproduce attach jitter in staging.
mika: will follow up with a short doc and a playbook for rollback/scale in the incident ticket.
oncall: closing slack triage for now, will reopen if evictions climb again. :lock:
